newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha meeting to discuss S.Korea status.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha meeting to discuss S.Korea status.

text.p: One of the major topics at this year's open-spec naphtha conference starting in Tokyo on Monday will be a possible transition of South Korea from a buyer of open-spec cargoes to a supplier, traders said on Monday.
Open-spec naphtha is currently traded on a C-and-F (cost and freight) Japan or South Korea basis, which makes the two east Asian countries exclusive end-users of open-spec cargoes.

However, some oil firms in South Korea are seeking to participate in the Asia's benchmark forward contract trading as cargo suppliers rather than importers as the country's refining capacity expands, traders said.

Currently South Korea can play only a buyer's role under the terms of the contract, although oil firms and petrochemical manufacturers in the country in fact rarely buy cargoes from the open-spec naphtha chain, they said.
The two-day conference is expected to slow down naphtha trading in Asia temporarily as most of the region's major naphtha dealers are likely to attend, the traders added.
